text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- A businessman was seriously injured in a bomb blast, the was the third attempt on his life. Police consider this a conflict between criminal figures.
- Negotiations for the expansion of the ruling coalition are going on but potential allies are still hesitating.
- The government increased the minimum wage from 680 to 845 kroons.
- The State Court sentenced its first criminal to life imprisonment, a 24-year-old man who had killed four people.
- Parliament is currently debating a draft law on artificial insemination and protection of embryos.
- Foreign ministry vice-chancellor Mati Vaarmann will become Estonia's next ambassador to Finland.

- The government will approve an agreement on visa-free travel with Sweden next week. The agreement should be signed in mid-March and come into force on May 1, coinciding with visa-free travel agreements with Finland and Norway.
- The Fatherland Union and Moderate parties announced that they will remain in opposition.
- The police have hastily formed a team for combatting pickpockets. The move was influenced by a shooting incident in central Tallinn, when a citizen and a thief were wounded.
- Estonians in Sweden have expressed their dissatisfaction with the president's late arrival to Independence Day meeting last week. Meri was 40 minutes late.
- Illegal labour in the building business is three times cheaper than registered building firms.
- The southern Estonian Tartu furniture plant Tarmeko has formed a joint venture in Ukraine for the export of furniture.
